content.user_title: Verify Rust Proofs and SMT Queries with Sail
content.value_statement: Repeated Verus checks and SMT queries can slow proof development and complicate evidence tracking. This skill guides Sail workflows for cached verification, repair validation, and accurate result interpretation.
actual_capabilities: Guide Cargo project verification with Sail and interpret failure diagnostics.
Explain proof-repair checks that require a full-target verification result.
Guide complete SMT-LIB requests through bundled Z3 with cached decided results.
Distinguish verification freshness, result scope, and proof success.
Describe CLI and MCP workflows for background verification jobs.
Explain release-dependent standalone verification and cache management.
limitations: Requires an installed Sail runtime on Linux x86-64 or Apple-silicon macOS.
Standalone verification and cache budget commands depend on the installed Sail release.
Proof-repair validation requires the interactive engine; the agent must write the candidate repair.
SMT answers apply only to submitted formulas; partial or historical verification does not establish a current full-target proof.

use_cases.title: Iterate on Rust contracts
use_cases.description: Use Sail diagnostics and reusable solver work while developing Verus proofs without weakening intended contracts.

use_cases.title: Validate automated proof repairs
use_cases.description: Check candidate repairs, inspect completed jobs, and require current full-target success before accepting changes.

use_cases.title: Repeat constraint checks
use_cases.description: Submit complete SMT-LIB transcripts, inspect models or unsat cores, and reuse matching decided results.

prompt_templates.title: Verify an existing project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Sail to verify this Cargo/Verus project. Report the verdict, checked scope, freshness, and failure diagnostics.

prompt_templates.title: Run an SMT query
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Sail runtime capabilities, then run my SMT-LIB transcript. Report each satisfiability result, requested model or core, and cache reuse.

prompt_templates.title: Check a candidate proof repair
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate my candidate repair for [package] and [function] with Sail. Preserve the contract and require current full-target success before accepting it.

prompt_templates.title: Track background verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the configured Sail MCP server to submit background verification for [project]. Inspect installed schemas, read the completed result, and report scope and freshness.

output_examples.input: Illustrate a report for a focused proof check that passes without full-target evidence.
output_examples.output: The selected function passed. Full-target verification has not completed, so the repair remains provisional.

output_examples.input: Illustrate a result summary for a cached SMT query requiring an integer greater than two.
output_examples.output: The formula is satisfiable. The returned model assigns an integer greater than two. The result reports a cache hit for this matching request.

output_examples.input: Illustrate a report when successful verification predates source changes.
output_examples.output: The earlier result was successful but is now Historical. Verify the current inputs again before reporting a current proof.

best_practices: Check installed help, MCP schemas, and release compatibility before choosing a workflow.
Require the correct scope, a successful verdict, and Current evidence before accepting verification.
Keep logs and transcripts outside watched inputs, and preserve intended contracts during repairs.
anti_patterns: Accepting a focused function pass as proof that the entire target verifies.
Treating runtime readiness, Unknown results, or timeouts as successful solver evidence.
Weakening contracts to hide implementation failures.

faq.question: Which systems does Sail support?
faq.answer: The skill documents Linux x86-64 and Apple-silicon macOS.

faq.question: Does this skill include Sail, Verus, or Z3?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance. Sail must be installed separately and ships its own Verus and Z3.

faq.question: Can I use an existing Verus project?
faq.answer: Yes. Sail accepts Cargo Verus verification arguments. Check compatibility and use Cargo directly when your project requires a different Verus release.

faq.question: Does Current mean verification succeeded?
faq.answer: No. Current describes evidence freshness. Read the verdict and checked scope separately.

faq.question: When can SMT output be reused?
faq.answer: Sail reuses decided output when transcript bytes, limits, pinned solver identity, and execution settings match. Incomplete runs are not successful evidence.

faq.question: Can I use Sail through MCP?
faq.answer: Yes, with a configured Sail MCP server. Inspect installed tool schemas and read completed job results before reporting success.
